description: Original fictional evidence learning examples authored for ModuleMate. All passages and questions belonging to a document stay in one split. Positives require every listed gold passage; related text alone is not a complete answer. Generated negatives are local or from other documents in the same split. Small synthetic diagnostic, not representative user data.

passages.text: The Forge workshop runs on 6 March in Cedar Room. The morning session starts at 09:40.
A seat costs 7 tokens. Visitors may watch the demonstration for free, but watching does not reserve a seat.
Participants must bring closed shoes. Gloves are supplied. A personal drill is optional.
A participant can transfer a booking after notifying the organiser. The note gives no refund deadline.

questions.text: Where is the Forge workshop held?
How much does a seat at the Forge workshop cost?
Does a Forge participant have to bring gloves?
Can I give my Forge booking to someone else?
Give the Forge workshop location and seat price.
What is the last date to request a Forge refund?
Where is Forge held and who founded it?

passages.text: A limpet scrapes algae from the rock using a toothed feeding structure called a radula.
The observation team counted animals in square frames of equal area. The count alone is not a measurement of animal mass.
Keep the sampling area constant when comparing counts from different shore levels. Record the tide and time.
The notes name no predator of the observed limpets and contain no population estimate for the whole coast.

questions.text: What do the observed limpets eat?
Did the tide pool team measure animal weight?
What should stay the same when comparing shore counts?
Do the field notes estimate the entire coastal population?
Explain how limpets feed and how the team counted animals.
Which bird hunted the limpets?
Describe the sampling method and give the measured salinity.

passages.text: The helper stores a result under a string key after computing it. A later lookup of the same key returns the stored value.
Deleting a key removes its saved value. It does not erase entries under other keys.
The cache has a limit of 40 entries. When full, it removes the least recently accessed entry before inserting a new one.
The example runs inside one process. It does not describe disk persistence or concurrent access.

questions.text: What happens when the Cache helper sees a key again?
Does deleting one Cache helper key clear every entry?
Which entry is removed when the Cache helper fills up?
Does this cache survive a program restart?
Describe lookup reuse and the Cache helper capacity.
How many worker threads can safely write to the cache?
Explain cache deletion and name its database engine.

passages.text: The Maple reading room lends printed books for 18 days. Reference atlases remain in the room.
A borrower may renew once if nobody has reserved the book. A reservation prevents renewal even before the due date.
Returning a book after 17:00 records the return on the next opening day. The return box is beside the west door.
The notice does not state a late-return fine. It gives an email address for questions about accessibility.

questions.text: How long can I borrow a Maple printed book?
Can I renew a reserved Maple book?
Where is the Maple book return box?
What happens if I return a Maple book after five in the afternoon?
Give the Maple loan period and renewal condition.
What is the Maple late-return charge?
Where is the return box and who manages the reading room?

passages.text: A layer of pale volcanic ash lies above the dark clay in the fictional sample. In this undisturbed sequence, the upper ash was deposited later.
The glass fragments in the ash are angular. The note describes their shape, not a measured cooling rate.
Two samples can be compared using both mineral composition and position in the sequence. Similar colour alone does not establish a match.
No numerical age or eruption date was measured for these layers.

questions.text: Which came first in the sample, dark clay or pale ash?
What shape are the ash glass fragments?
Is matching colour enough to identify the same ash layer?
Which layer lies above the clay?
Describe the layer order and the recommended comparison evidence.
In what year did the ash eruption occur?
Describe the glass shape and calculate the cooling speed.

passages.text: The Birch shuttle leaves the museum stop at 10:10 and reaches the orchard stop at 10:35 on its published route.
A single journey costs 3 credits. Children under six travel without a fare when accompanied by an adult.
Bicycles are accepted only when the rear rack has space. Buying a ticket does not reserve bicycle space.
The leaflet gives no timetable for public holidays and no contact name for the driver.

questions.text: When does the Birch shuttle reach the orchard?
Does a five-year-old with an adult need a Birch fare?
Does a Birch ticket guarantee space for my bicycle?
How much is a Birch single journey?
Give the museum departure time and the bicycle condition.
What is the Birch public-holiday timetable?
What is the fare and what is the driver's name?

passages.text: The soil sensor uses two AA cells. Insert both with the polarity shown inside the compartment.
A slow amber flash indicates low charge. A steady amber light indicates that pairing is in progress.
Disconnect external power before opening the battery compartment. The enclosure should remain dry during replacement.
The guide supplies no battery-life estimate and does not specify a rechargeable-cell brand.

questions.text: How many cells power the soil sensor?
What does a slowly flashing amber sensor light mean?
What must I disconnect before replacing sensor cells?
Does a steady amber light mean low charge?
Name the required cells and the replacement precaution.
How many months will the sensor batteries last?
Describe the pairing light and name the recommended charger.

passages.text: The first Stoneford crossing was a wooden footbridge completed in 1842. The stone replacement opened in 1870.
The drawing dated 1838 is a proposal, not a record of a finished bridge. Its designer is not identified.
The old timber footbridge was dismantled after the replacement opened. The two structures were not open together afterward.
The local account does not give either bridge's construction cost.

questions.text: When did the stone Stoneford replacement open?
Does the 1838 drawing prove the Stoneford bridge was finished then?
What happened to the timber bridge after the replacement opened?
Was the first Stoneford crossing made of stone?
Contrast the proposal date and the replacement opening date.
Who drew the Stoneford proposal?
Give the first bridge's material and its construction budget.

passages.text: The repair bench accepts lamps and small radios. It does not accept microwave ovens.
Book a 25-minute slot before visiting. A booking covers inspection, not a promise that the device will be repaired.
Owners must bring the power cable if the device uses a detachable cable. Replacement parts are charged separately.
No fixed price list or warranty duration is published in these rules.

questions.text: Can I take a microwave to the repair bench?
Does a repair bench booking guarantee a successful fix?
What should I bring for a device with a detachable cable?
How long is a repair bench appointment?
List accepted devices and explain what a booking covers.
How long is the repair warranty?
Explain the cable requirement and state the exact inspection fee.

passages.text: Mix 60 grams of oats with 120 millilitres of milk in a clean jar. The quantities are for one jar.
Leave the covered jar in a refrigerator overnight. The instructions do not call for cooking the oats.
Add the chopped pear just before serving so it retains its texture. Cinnamon is optional.
The recipe gives no calorie count and does not describe a milk-free substitute.

questions.text: How much milk goes into one oat jar?
Do the oat jar instructions require cooking?
When should I add the pear to the oat jar?
Is cinnamon compulsory in the oat jar?
Give the oat amount and explain the overnight storage.
How many calories are in the oat jar?
Give the pear timing and a tested dairy-free replacement.

passages.text: A radio pulse carries information by varying a property of a carrier wave. In the example, amplitude is varied while carrier frequency stays fixed.
The receiver compares the incoming amplitude with a reference level. A larger recorded amplitude does not by itself establish a more distant transmitter.
The exercise asks students to sketch amplitude against time. Label the vertical axis in arbitrary units.
No numeric wave speed or transmitter distance is supplied.

questions.text: Which carrier property varies in the radio example?
Does a larger received amplitude prove the transmitter is farther away?
What belongs on the vertical axis of the radio sketch?
Is the carrier frequency changing in this example?
Describe the modulation and the requested sketch axes.
How far away is the radio transmitter?
Identify the changing property and calculate propagation time.

passages.text: Mira found a silver envelope inside the library's returned atlas. She left it unopened on the librarian's desk.
The librarian, Oren, read the address and put the envelope in the outgoing post tray. Mira did not read the letter.
The final scene takes place that evening at the closed library door. Rain begins after Oren locks it.
The story leaves the sender unnamed and does not explain why the envelope was inside the atlas.

questions.text: Where did Mira find the silver envelope?
Who placed the silver envelope in the post tray?
Did Mira read the silver letter?
When did the rain begin in the silver envelope story?
Describe Mira's discovery and Oren's response.
Why had the sender hidden the envelope in the atlas?
Name the librarian and explain the sender's childhood.

passages.text: The sample uses linen for the lengthwise warp and wool for the crosswise weft. The note distinguishes thread position from fibre type.
Pass the shuttle through the open shed, then beat the new weft into place. Beating happens after the shuttle pass.
A broken warp thread must be repaired before continuing. Changing the weft colour is optional.
The note contains no finished cloth dimensions or estimate of sale price.

questions.text: Which fibre forms the warp of the weaving sample?
When is the weft beaten into place?
Can I continue the weaving sample with a broken warp?
Is changing the weft colour required?
Identify the warp and describe the shuttle sequence.
How wide is the completed linen cloth?
Explain warp repair and give the finished sale price.

passages.text: The Cove cleanup meets at South Pier at 08:20 on 19 May. Teams leave the pier together.
Volunteers sort rope and plastic into separate bags. Sharp objects should be reported to the team leader rather than picked up.
Participation is free. Volunteers under sixteen must work beside their registered guardian.
The notice does not name the sponsor or state a maximum number of volunteers.

questions.text: Where do Cove cleanup teams meet?
What should a Cove volunteer do with a sharp object?
Can a fifteen-year-old join Cove without a guardian?
Is there a Cove participation charge?
Give the Cove meeting time and the sorting instructions.
Who sponsors the Cove cleanup?
State the meeting point and the total volunteer capacity.

passages.text: The poem 'Lantern at Dawn' is attributed to the fictional writer Sela Venn. Its speaker watches a neighbour carry a lantern.
The final stanza repeats the opening image with a change from darkness to dawn. Repetition connects the beginning and ending.
The notes describe the lantern as an image of companionship. They do not identify the speaker as the author.
No publication year or biographical birthplace is given.

questions.text: Who wrote Lantern at Dawn according to the notes?
How does the last stanza connect to the opening?
Do the notes say the poem's speaker is its author?
What meaning do the notes associate with the lantern?
Name the attributed writer and explain the repeated image.
In which city was Sela Venn born?
Explain the lantern image and give the first publication date.

passages.text: Root the mint cuttings in moist compost under bright indirect light. Each cutting should have at least one leaf node below the surface.
Keep the compost damp rather than waterlogged. A transparent cover reduces moisture loss but must allow ventilation.
New roots may form before visible new leaves appear. A leaf count alone is not a direct measurement of root length.
The nursery note provides no measured rooting times or recommended fertiliser dosage.

questions.text: Where should the mint cutting's leaf node be placed?
Should the cutting compost be flooded with water?
Does counting new leaves measure mint root length?
What lighting does the mint cutting note recommend?
Explain moisture management and the cover's purpose.
How many days will these mint cuttings take to root?
Describe the compost conditions and give the fertiliser dose.

passages.text: The parcel prototype must accept a tracking code and show the last stored scan. Live carrier integration is optional.
A scan record includes a timestamp and location. The timestamp records a scan, not a promised delivery time.
The prototype review is on 22 August. The source archive is due on 20 August, two days before the review.
The brief does not select a framework, database or hosting provider.

questions.text: Does the parcel prototype require live carrier integration?
Does the parcel scan timestamp promise delivery then?
When is the parcel source archive due?
What fields belong in a stored parcel scan?
Describe the required tracking feature and the review date.
Which database must the parcel team use?
Give the archive deadline and the hosting budget.

passages.text: The Dome session observes Jupiter on 11 January, starting at 19:30. Meet at the north entrance of the observatory.
Use the low-power eyepiece first to locate the planet. Increase magnification only after the object is centred.
The session costs 5 tokens. Members aged twelve or older may attend without a guardian; younger members need an accompanying adult.
The card gives no weather forecast or distance measurement for Jupiter.

questions.text: At which entrance should Dome observers meet?
Which eyepiece should Dome observers use first?
May an eleven-year-old attend Dome alone?
How much does the Dome session cost?
Give the Dome starting time and explain the eyepiece order.
Will the sky be clear during Dome?
Give the session price and Jupiter's measured distance.

passages.text: The Reed ensemble rehearses in Studio Four at 18:15 every Thursday. The notice concerns rehearsals, not public concerts.
Players should tune before the first group exercise. The leader starts with a slow unison phrase, then separates the parts.
Bring a music stand and pencil. Printed scores are supplied, so players do not need to print their own.
The notice does not name a concert venue or list membership fees.

questions.text: Where does the Reed ensemble rehearse?
What happens before Reed separates into parts?
Must Reed players print their own scores?
What should I bring to Reed rehearsal?
Give the rehearsal day and describe the first group exercise.
How much does Reed membership cost?
Name the rehearsal room and the public concert venue.

passages.text: Pour cloudy water through the gravel and sand layers into a clean collecting cup. The filter traps some suspended solid particles.
Clear-looking filtered water is not proof that the water is safe to drink. The demonstration does not remove every dissolved substance.
Measure the collected volume using a graduated cylinder. Compare the same starting volume in repeated trials.
The demonstration sheet supplies no dissolved-salt concentration or bacterial test results.

questions.text: What does the sand filter trap?
Can I assume clear sand-filtered water is safe to drink?
How should the collected filter volume be measured?
Does the sand demonstration remove every dissolved substance?
Explain the filter's purpose and a fair repeated-trial condition.
What is the filtered water's dissolved salt concentration?
Describe the volume measurement and report the bacterial count.

passages.text: The archive portal lets a reader search catalogue titles and request a scan. A request is reviewed by staff before any scan is released.
Digital scans are delivered through the reader's inbox. A printed copy can be collected by arrangement but is optional.
Readers may submit three pending requests at once. Completing a request frees one place; there is no stated lifetime request limit.
The guide does not state a response-time guarantee or identify the scanning software.

questions.text: Does submitting an archive request immediately release a scan?
Are printed archive copies mandatory?
How many archive requests can be pending together?
Where are digital archive scans delivered?
Describe scan approval and the pending-request limit.
Which program does the archive use to scan?
Explain digital delivery and state the guaranteed response time.

passages.text: The Frost market opens at 11:20 on 8 December in Willow Square. Stallholders may enter one hour before visitors.
A craft stall costs 9 credits. General visitors pay no entry fee.
Stallholders must bring their own table. A canopy is optional unless a later weather notice requires one.
The notice gives no closing time or cancellation refund policy.

questions.text: Where does the Frost market take place?
Do Frost visitors pay the craft stall fee?
Must Frost stallholders bring a table?
Is a canopy always required at Frost?
Give the Frost visitor opening time and craft stall cost.
When does Frost close?
Give the table requirement and the refund conditions.
